rationale: The captured context from NASA Langley's DASC 2024 presentation (S-EVID-005, PDF pp. 5-8) directly formalizes the Plaidypvs RTA rule for a black-box controller alpha and reversionary controller beta. The rule establishes the safety property S ('for all runs of the system, the safety property S is satisfied') only IF the vehicle starts in a safe state, the monitored advanced system controller always ends in a state where the vehicle can recover, and repeated execution of the reversionary system controller leads to a safe state, with explicit monitor sample-rate/timing (tau, M) and carry-over state (G) premises.
evidence_locators: S-EVID-005-R1 (PDF pp. 5-8, Simplex architecture and Plaidypvs rule)
S-EVID-005-R2 (PDF pp. 8-12, RTA premises and productive-conflict-avoidance example)
limitations: The source is a research conference presentation and formalization framework, not a civil aviation airworthiness certification or implementation safety case.
The formal proof assumes monitor observability and validity of plant dynamics bounds; it does not solve common-cause perception failures where the monitor shares an unobserved hazard.
